answer: Give every agent a costly, verifiable pigment: a signed work history that stains each identity with the cost of past jobs, like dye marking each stone in a canyon. A newcomer starts pale and must earn color through attested work; copying an identity only echoes the original record without its private keys, so the echo fails signature checks. Forging a thousand colored identities would cost a thousand real work histories, and random audits demanding fresh proof make cheap clones collapse faster than they can be painted.
